title: Levofloxacin-Induced Eosinophilic Pneumonia with Systemic Manifestations: A Case Report and Literature Review
Your Future Is a Mirrored Cage: Sycophancy, Middlestack Mutability, and the Infrastructure of Personalized Hate
YAŞAR KEMAL’İN TENEKE ROMANINI WEBER’İN RASYONALİTESİ İLE MİLL’İN LİBERALİZMİ IŞIĞINDA TARİHSEL-SİYASAL PERSPEKTİFTEN OKUMAK
journal: International Journal Of Turkish Literature Culture Education
abstract: Yaşar Kemal’in Teneke romanı, 1950’li yılların Türkiye’sinde yükselen sermaye odaklı tarım burjuvazisi ile modern / rasyonel hukuk bürokrasisi arasındaki gerilimi merkezine alır. Roman, rasyonel bürokrasiyi ve yasalara sadakati temsil eden idealist Kaymakam Fikret Irmaklı’nın, millî kalkınma retoriğiyle yasaları fiilen geçersiz kılan yerel elitler (çeltik ağaları) karşısındaki mücadelesini ve yenilgisini konu eder.Bu çalışma, romanı Weber’in rasyonel-yasal bürokrasi teorisi ve Mill’in liberalizm anlayışı çerçevesinde, tarihsel-politik bir perspektifle analiz etmekte; devletin tarafsız bir araç olmaktan çıkarılıp yerel elitlerin çıkarlarına tabi kılındığı bir dönemin zihniyet yapısını Resul Efendi’nin sinmiş memur tipolojisi ve Fikret Irmaklı’nın tasfiye edilen idealizmi üzerinden çözümlemektedir. Çalışma, kuramsal çerçeve ile vaka analizini bütünleştirerek romanı yalnızca estetik bir nesne olarak değil, tarihsel bağlamı içinde dönemi aydınlatan bir belge, aynı zamanda siyaset bilimi ve kamu yönetimi kuramlarının sınandığı ve somutlaştırıldığı bir inceleme alanı olarak değerlendirmektedir.

title: Utilising the binary in situ nanostructuring strategy of nanosilica/nanoalumina for long-term optimisation in high-dosage cement composites
abstract: The in situ growth of nanoparticles (NPs) on host surfaces has emerged as an advanced approach to enhance the performance of cementitious composites. However, the practical use of in situ grown NPs is limited by agglomeration and poor reactivity at dosages above 0.5%, restricting long-term reinforcement. That limitation was overcome in this work, enabling effective use of NPs at dosages of 1–2%. Highly dispersed in situ grown nanosilica (INS) and γ-nanoalumina (INA) were incorporated into cement composites (ICs) and compared with commercial NP composites (CCs) at identical dosages. The workability, hydration kinetics, mechanical properties, drying shrinkage behaviour, carbonation resistance and microstructural characteristics were evaluated up to 90 days. The IC samples exhibited excellent dispersion and minimal fluidity loss (–5.2% to –22.4%), whereas the CCs showed significant fluidity loss. The dual nucleation and dual pozzolanic activity of INS and INA accelerated hydration and sustained strength gain, with IC 1.0 (2 wt% NPs) achieving 14.1% higher 90-day compressive strength than the reference. The ICs also showed reduced early shrinkage, lower carbonation depth and refined pore structures (critical pore size of 6.8 nm for IC 0.5). These results indicate that binary in situ nanostructuring enables efficient, high-dosage NP utilisation, producing dense and high-performance cement composites with improved shrinkage behaviour and carbonation resistance.

title: United Nations Peacekeeping in Africa: Evolution, Operational Experience and Lessons from Major Peace Operations
journal: Frontline Social Sciences and History Journal
abstract: United Nations peacekeeping in Africa has evolved from ceasefire monitoring into multidimensional intervention encompassing civilian protection, political transition, electoral assistance, disarmament and post-conflict peacebuilding. Yet broader mandates have produced markedly different outcomes across missions. This paper examines the evolution and operational experience of UN peacekeeping through a comparative analysis of operations in Namibia, Mozambique, Rwanda, Somalia, Angola and Burundi. It considers how political and operational conditions interacted to shape mission outcomes, focusing on commitment to negotiated settlements, acceptance of electoral outcomes, mandate credibility, management of spoilers, disarmament, regional cooperation and sustained international engagement. The comparison shows that Namibia and Mozambique benefited from conditions that enabled peacekeeping to reinforce viable political settlements and support the movement of political competition from armed confrontation into institutional processes. Rwanda demonstrates the consequences of inadequate capability and political commitment in a rapidly deteriorating security environment, while Somalia illustrates the limitations of coercive intervention in the absence of a viable political settlement. Angola highlights the fragility of peace implementation when powerful actors retain military alternatives to electoral competition, whereas Burundi demonstrates the contribution of multidimensional peacekeeping within a longer process of domestic negotiation and regional engagement. The paper argues that the evolution of UN peacekeeping in Africa is better understood through the relationship between political settlement and operational intervention than through mandate expansion alone. Durable outcomes are more likely where political commitment, credible mandates, operational capacity and regional support reinforce one another. These findings underline the need for politically grounded and operationally realistic peacekeeping strategies capable of supporting institutions that can sustain peaceful political competition beyond mission withdrawal.

title: Undifferentiated Small Round Cell Sarcoma of the Pelvic Space in an Infant: A Rare Case Report
journal: Undifferentiated Small Round Cell Sarcoma of the Pelvic Space in an Infant: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Undifferentiated small round cell sarcomas (USRCS) are rare high-grade malignancies, which are even more exceptional when arising in the retroperitoneal space in infancy, with fewer than 100 such cases documented worldwide. We report a 4-month-old infant who presented with an incidentally detected lower abdominal mass. Imaging, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry (IHC) established a diagnosis of USRCS. The patient was managed with multimodal therapy comprising neoadjuvant vincristine, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide alternating with ifosfamide and etoposide (VDC/IE) chemotherapy, surgical excision with right pelvic lymph node dissection, adjuvant radiotherapy, and further chemotherapy. This case underscores the rarity of pelvic USRCS in infancy, the diagnostic complexity posed by coexisting conditions, and the necessity of a multimodal diagnostic and therapeutic approach.

The right to remain: touristification, social sustainability and the governance of living heritage in Cádiz
journal: Journal of Cultural Heritage Management and Sustainable Development
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how a flagship living-heritage festival is governed under touristification pressures and what this means for the social sustainability of a mature urban destination. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative case study of the Cádiz Carnival during the 2025 festival cycle. It combines participant observation, 10 semi-structured interviews with actors in the carnival field, and critical discourse analysis of a focal corpus of eight carnival group repertoires. Findings The findings show how heritage recognition, tourism visibility and spatial regulation intersect around participation, access to public space and residentiality. Five recurring tensions structure this governance: safeguarding and intergenerational transmission; professionalisation and mediated legitimacy; tourism-driven pressures on mobility, crowding and housing; the vernacular work of critique and symbolic boundary-making in song lyrics; and contested imaginaries of the festival's future. Carnival lyrics function as vernacular public commentary and as a feedback infrastructure for destination governance, making everyday inequalities legible and linking tourism growth to resident liveability. Practical implications The paper suggests that safeguarding intangible cultural heritage in tourist cities requires governance approaches that connect heritage policy with public-space management, housing pressures and everyday urban infrastructures. Social implications The social sustainability of living heritage depends on protecting residents' capacity to remain, participate and reproduce cultural practices in place. Originality/value The paper shifts debate beyond authenticity by showing that the key issue is the set of urban, residential and participatory conditions that sustain living heritage under touristification. It also advances the analysis of carnival lyrics as a situated vernacular corpus through which communities publicly narrate, evaluate and contest tourism-led urban change.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on supply chain finance: a multi-methods approach
journal: The International Journal of Logistics Management
abstract: Purpose Despite the growing importance of supply chain finance (SCF) in global business operations, current research lacks a comprehensive understanding of how diverse stakeholders perceive, prioritize and engage with SCF mechanisms. This study addresses this gap by applying stakeholder theory to develop a multi-stakeholder perspective on SCF themes, tensions and value creation dynamics. Design/methodology/approach We employ a two-phase sequential mixed-methods design. Phase 1 utilizes Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) techniques to analyze 288 academic articles and social media content (blogs, forums and industry reports) to identify key SCF themes. Phase 2 involves 18 semi-structured interviews with SCF stakeholders (academic experts, practitioners, financial institution representatives and technology providers) to capture stakeholder-specific perspectives and tensions. Data triangulation integrates insights across all sources, analyzed through a stakeholder theory lens using the Antecedents–Decisions–Outcomes (ADO) framework. Findings Six key themes emerge: (1) Risk Management in SCF, (2) Financial Strategies and Working Capital Management, (3) Sustainability and Resilience, (4) Digital Transformation and Technology, (5) Economic and Geopolitical Factors and (6) Responsible Financing and Ethical Considerations. Analysis reveals significant convergence between academic and practitioner perspectives on established themes (risk, finance and technology) but notable divergence on emerging concerns (geopolitical factors and ethical financing). Seven theoretical propositions are developed explaining stakeholder salience, tension dynamics and value creation mechanisms. Critical findings include: (1) stakeholder power-urgency mismatches inhibit digital transformation, (2) efficiency-ethics tensions vary by stakeholder salience and (3) geopolitical shocks reveal latent stakeholder conflicts. Originality/value This study makes three primary contributions. Theoretically, it is the first to apply stakeholder theory to multi-theme SCF analysis, developing propositions about stakeholder dynamics that extend beyond dyadic buyer-supplier relationships. Empirically, it triangulates academic literature, social media data and stakeholder interviews to reveal perspective gaps between researchers and practitioners. Methodologically, it demonstrates how data triangulation can identify emerging constructs (geopolitical risk, responsible financing) before they receive substantial academic attention. Practically, it provides stakeholder-specific recommendations for managing tensions and creating shared value in SCF networks.
